summary: The four exact round-1 malformed v3 execution cases are fixed, but LIVE-03 remains open for incomplete validation of the surrounding v3 result shape, role/identifier primitives and reference arrays. The bounded inventory reproduces 20 container/element tracebacks and 22 false accepts. These accesses were inherited from the shared result validator, not introduced by round 2. The explicit result/pair/arm/execution guards and three nonblank-string fields work. Independent checks of the remaining same-boundary surface reveal inherited unguarded routing/worker/check/scorer access, truthiness-based role/identifier/model acceptance, and set-coercion of non-array references. open_errors.summary: V3 only partially validates its result structure: nested nonobjects crash, truthy non-string role/identifier/model values pass, and string/object references are accepted as arrays.
open_errors.violated_contract: R-059's evidence-bearing scored native-result boundary and the v3 protocol's retained routing/check/scorer/operational schema and evidence-reference validation. These are container and primitive type errors, not disputed evidence authenticity, calendar semantics or broader live-task quality.
open_errors.cause: V3 guards the immediate execution structure but falls through into shared v2-era code that dereferences routing, worker, check and scorer before proving object shape, tests worker role/requested_model and scorer.id only by truthiness, and converts reference fields with set() without proving a string-array type. The malformed accesses predate this round; the new repair did not introduce them.

observed_groups.behavior: routing, worker element, check element and scorer set separately to null, true, 1, a string or an array each produce exit 1 with AttributeError instead of structured exit 2.

scorer.id, treatment worker.role and treatment worker.requested_model set separately to true, 1, a nonempty array or object each return exit 0 with ok:true. Properly validated evidence/command IDs and effective-model fields reject corresponding wrong types.

Check, score, scorer, operational and non-null-usage references accept an object mapping existing reference IDs to true (five cases). They also accept the string x after a legitimate one-character evidence ID x is added (five cases), because set('x') equals {'x'}. The equivalent ['x'] positive controls pass. Native completion and command reference fields correctly reject the non-array string.

Cover the 25 targets listed in surface-summary.json, the seven primitive fields and reference branches in primitive-summary.json, and the original four fixed inputs. Every retained malformed case must reject with one JSON error and exit 2; no false acceptance, traceback or blanket exception masking. Explicitly document the native result's container/primitive/reference shape where needed. Preserve successful evidenced null-native-exit results, valid reference arrays including one-character IDs, nullable unobserved effective identity/usage, integer subprocess exits and evidence/provenance/reference negative checks. Keep timestamp syntax/order outside this declared structural validator and leave frozen v2 behavior/protocol/rubric unchanged. A normal synthetic regression suite must exercise the complete bounded surface without importing old sandboxes.
